sanskrit: prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ abhyabhāṣata kākutsthaṃ śayānaṃ parṇasaṃstare
english: When the night had brightened into dawn, the great sage Viśvāmitra addressed Kākutstha (Rāma), who lay sleeping on a bed of leaves.

sanskrit: kausalyā suprajā rāma pūrvā saṃdhyā pravartate uttiṣṭha naraśārdūla kartavyaṃ daivam āhnikam
english: "Kausalyā is blessed with a noble son — O Rāma, the eastern twilight is beginning; arise, O tiger among men, and perform the daily divine rites."

sanskrit: tasyarṣeḥ paramodāraṃ vacaḥ śrutvā nṛpātmajau snātvā kṛtodakau vīrau jepatuḥ paramaṃ japam
english: Having heard those most gracious words of the sage, the two sons of the king — those heroes — bathed, performed their water-offerings, and recited the supreme prayer.

sanskrit: kṛtāhnikau mahāvīryau viśvāmitraṃ tapodhanam abhivādyābhisaṃhṛṣṭau gamanāyopatasthatuḥ
english: Having completed the morning rites, those two of great valour saluted Viśvāmitra, the treasure of austerity, and, greatly delighted, presented themselves ready to depart.

sanskrit: tau prayāte mahāvīryau divyaṃ tripathagāṃ nadīm dadṛśāte tatas tatra sarayvāḥ saṃgame śubhe
english: As those two of great valour set out, they beheld there the divine river that flows in three paths (the Gaṅgā), at her auspicious confluence with the Sarayū.

sanskrit: tatrāśramapadaṃ puṇyam ṛṣīṇām ugratejasām bahuvarṣasahasrāṇi tapyatāṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ
english: There was a holy hermitage of sages of fierce splendour who had been performing the highest austerity for many thousands of years.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaprītau rāghavau puṇyam āśramam ūcatus taṃ mahātmānaṃ viśvāmitram idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Seeing that holy hermitage, the two Rāghavas were filled with the deepest joy, and they spoke these words to the great-souled Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: kasyāyam āśramaḥ puṇyaḥ ko nv asmin vasate pumān bhagavañ śrotum icchāvaḥ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi nau
english: "Whose is this holy hermitage, O Blessed One, and what man dwells here? We wish to hear — great is our curiosity."

sanskrit: tayos tad vacanaṃ śrutvā prahasya munipuṃgavaḥ abravīc chrūyatāṃ rāma yasyāyaṃ pūrva āśramaḥ
english: Hearing their words, the foremost of sages smiled and spoke: "Listen, O Rāma, to whose this hermitage formerly belonged."

sanskrit: kandarpo mūrtimān āsīt kāma ity ucyate budhaiḥ
english: "Kandarpa — he who is called Kāma (Love) by the wise — once existed here in embodied form."

sanskrit: tapasyantam iha sthāṇuṃ niyamena samāhitam kṛtodvāhaṃ tu deveśaṃ gacchantaṃ samarudgaṇam dharṣayām āsa durmedhā huṃkṛtaś ca mahātmanā
english: "The foolish one (Kāma) dared to assail Sthāṇu (Śiva), who was here performing austerity, collected in discipline, even as the lord of the gods was departing with his wedding train together with the host of Maruts; and that great-souled one (Śiva) uttered a wrathful exclamation."

sanskrit: dagdhasya tasya raudreṇa cakṣuṣā raghunandana vyaśīryanta śarīrāt svāt sarvagātrāṇi durmateḥ
english: "Burned by that terrible eye (of Śiva), O joy of the Raghu line, all the limbs fell from the body of that foolish one."

sanskrit: tasya gātraṃ hataṃ tatra nirdagdhasya mahātmanā aśarīraḥ kṛtaḥ kāmaḥ krodhād deveśvareṇa ha
english: "His body destroyed, utterly burned by that great-souled one, Kāma was made bodiless there by the lord of the gods in his wrath."

sanskrit: anaṅga iti vikhyātas tadā prabhṛti rāghava sa cāṅgaviṣayaḥ śrīmān yatrāṅgaṃ sa mumoca ha
english: "From that time onward, O Rāghava, he became renowned as Anaṅga ('the bodiless'); and that prosperous region where he abandoned his body is called the Aṅga country."

sanskrit: tasyāyam āśramaḥ puṇyas tasyeme munayaḥ purā śiṣyā dharmaparā vīra teṣāṃ pāpaṃ na vidyate
english: "This is his holy hermitage; these sages here were formerly his disciples, devoted to righteousness, O hero — no sin exists in them."

sanskrit: ihādya rajanīṃ rāma vasema śubhadarśana puṇyayoḥ saritor madhye śvas tariṣyāmahe vayam
english: "Let us stay here tonight, O Rāma of auspicious appearance, between these two holy rivers; tomorrow we shall cross over."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃvadatāṃ tatra tapo dīrgheṇa cakṣuṣā vijñāya paramaprītā munayo harṣam āgaman
english: As they were thus conversing there, the sages, perceiving them with the long sight of their austerity, came forward filled with the highest joy and delight.

sanskrit: arghyaṃ pādyaṃ tathātithyaṃ nivedyakuśikātmaje rāmalakṣmaṇayoḥ paścād akurvann atithikriyām
english: Offering the arghya (water for the guest's hands), pādya (water for the feet), and hospitality to the son of Kuśika (Viśvāmitra), they then performed the rites of hosting for Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: satkāraṃ samanuprāpya kathābhir abhirañjayan nyavasan susukhaṃ tatra kāmāśramapade tadā
english: Receiving that honourable welcome, they passed the time delightfully with stories and dwelt there in great happiness at the site of Kāma's hermitage.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhāte vimale kṛtāhnikam ariṃdamau viśvāmitraṃ puraskṛtya nadyās tīram upāgatau
english: Then, at the clear dawn, the two tamers of foes, having performed the morning rites, came to the bank of the river placing Viśvāmitra at their head.

sanskrit: te ca sarve mahātmāno munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ upasthāpya śubhāṃ nāvaṃ viśvāmitram athābruvan
english: All those great-souled sages of sharpened vows then drew up an auspicious boat and spoke to Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: ārohatu bhavān nāvaṃ rājaputrapuraskṛtaḥ ariṣṭaṃ gaccha panthānaṃ mā bhūt kālasya paryayaḥ
english: "Pray board the boat, preceded by the princes; go your way without mishap — let there be no reversal of time (delay)."

sanskrit: viśvāmitras tathety uktvā tān ṛṣīn abhipūjya ca tatāra sahitas tābhyāṃ saritaṃ sāgaraṃ gamām
english: Viśvāmitra said "So be it," honoured those sages, and crossed together with those two the river that flows to the ocean.

sanskrit: atha rāmaḥ sarinmadhye papraccha munipuṅgavam vāriṇo bhidyamānasya kim ayaṃ tumulo dhvaniḥ
english: Then in the middle of the river Rāma asked the foremost of sages: "What is this tumultuous sound of the water being cleft?"

sanskrit: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā kautūhala samanvitam kathayām āsa dharmātmā tasya śabdasya niścayam
english: Hearing the words of Rāghava filled with curiosity, the righteous-souled one explained the origin of that sound.

sanskrit: kailāsaparvate rāma manasā nirmitaṃ saraḥ brahmaṇā naraśārdūla tenedaṃ mānasaṃ saraḥ
english: "On Mount Kailāsa, O Rāma, Brahmā fashioned a lake by the power of his mind, O tiger among men; therefore this is called the Mānasa lake."

sanskrit: tasmāt susrāva sarasaḥ sāyodhyām upagūhate saraḥpravṛttā sarayūḥ puṇyā brahmasaraścyutā
english: "From that lake it flowed forth; it embraces Ayodhyā. The holy Sarayū, born from the lake, issued from Brahmā's lake."

sanskrit: tasyāyam atulaḥ śabdo jāhnavīm abhivartate vārisaṃkṣobhajo rāma praṇāmaṃ niyataḥ kuru
english: "This incomparable sound approaches the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā), born of the churning of the waters, O Rāma — bow in reverence without fail."

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ tu tāv ubhau kṛtvā praṇāmam atidhārmikau tīraṃ dakṣiṇam āsādya jagmatur laghuvikramau
english: Both of them, those two of surpassing righteousness, made their bow to the two rivers and, reaching the southern bank, proceeded with swift strides.

sanskrit: sa vanaṃ ghorasaṃkāśaṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpavarātmajaḥ aviprahatam aikṣvākaḥ papraccha munipuṃgavam
english: Seeing the forest of terrible aspect, the son of the best of kings, the Ikṣvāku prince (Rāma), unperturbed, asked the foremost of sages.

sanskrit: aho vanam idaṃ durgaṃ jhillikāgaṇanāditam bhairavaiḥ śvāpadaiḥ kīrṇaṃ śakuntair dāruṇārutaiḥ
english: "Ah, this forest is impenetrable, resounding with swarms of crickets, filled with fierce beasts of prey and birds with dreadful cries."

sanskrit: nānāprakāraiḥ śakunair vāśyadbhir bhairavasvanaiḥ siṃhavyāghravarāhaiś ca vāraṇaiś cāpi śobhitam
english: "It is thronged with various kinds of birds shrieking with frightful sounds, and graced with lions, tigers, wild boars, and elephants as well."

sanskrit: dhavāśvakarṇakakubhair bilvatindukapāṭalaiḥ saṃkīrṇaṃ badarībhiś ca kiṃ nv idaṃ dāruṇaṃ vanam
english: "It is crowded with dhava, aśvakarṇa, kakubha, bilva, tinduka, and pāṭala trees, and with jujube shrubs — what then is this fearful forest?"

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ śrūyatāṃ vatsa kākutstha yasyaitad dāruṇaṃ vanam
english: The great sage Viśvāmitra of great splendour said to him: "Hear, my child, O Kākutstha, to whom this fearful forest belongs."

sanskrit: etau janapadau sphītau pūrvam āstāṃ narottama maladāś ca karūṣāś ca devanirmāṇa nirmitau
english: "These two prosperous territories, O best of men — Maladā and Karūṣa — existed here formerly, fashioned by divine ordinance."

sanskrit: purā vṛtravadhe rāma malena samabhiplutam kṣudhā caiva sahasrākṣaṃ brahmahatyā yadāviśat
english: "Long ago, O Rāma, when the thousand-eyed Indra slew Vṛtra, he was overwhelmed with impurity and afflicted by hunger, and brahminicide entered him."

sanskrit: tam indraṃ snāpayan devā ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ kalaśaiḥ snāpayām āsur malaṃ cāsya pramocayan
english: "The gods and the sages, rich in austerity, bathed that Indra — they bathed him with their water-pots and released his impurity from him."

sanskrit: iha bhūmyāṃ malaṃ dattvā dattvā kāruṣam eva ca śarīrajaṃ mahendrasya tato harṣaṃ prapedire
english: "Having deposited the impurity and also the bile from Mahendra's body here upon this earth, they then attained joy."

sanskrit: nirmalo niṣkarūṣaś ca śucir indro yadābhavat dadau deśasya suprīto varaṃ prabhur anuttamam
english: "When Indra became pure, free of bile, and clean, the lord, greatly pleased, gave the region an unsurpassed boon."

sanskrit: imau janapadau sthītau khyātiṃ loke gamiṣyataḥ maladāś ca karūṣāś ca mamāṅgamaladhāriṇau
english: "'These two territories that bear the impurity and bile of my body — Maladā and Karūṣa — shall attain fame in the world.'"

sanskrit: sādhu sādhv iti taṃ devāḥ pākaśāsanam abruvan deśasya pūjāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtāṃ śakreṇa dhīmatā
english: "'Well done, well done!' — thus spoke the gods to Pākaśāsana (Indra), seeing that honour bestowed upon the region by wise Śakra."

sanskrit: etau janapadau sthītau dīrghakālam ariṃdama maladāś ca karūṣāś ca muditau dhanadhānyataḥ
english: "These two territories, Maladā and Karūṣa, O tamer of foes, flourished for a long time, rejoicing in wealth and grain."

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya yakṣī vai kāmarūpiṇī balaṃ nāgasahasrasya dhārayantī tadā hy abhūt
english: "Then, at a certain time, there was a yakṣī who could assume any form at will, bearing the strength of a thousand elephants."

sanskrit: tāṭakā nāma bhadraṃ te bhāryā sundasya dhīmataḥ mārīco rākṣasaḥ putro yasyāḥ śakraparākramaḥ
english: "Her name was Tāṭakā — blessings to you — the wife of the wise Sunda; her son was Mārīca, a rākṣasa of the valour of Śakra."

sanskrit: imau janapadau nityaṃ vināśayati rāghava maladāṃś ca karūṣāṃś ca tāṭakā duṣṭacāriṇī
english: "She, Tāṭakā of wicked conduct, perpetually destroys these two territories, O Rāghava — Maladā and Karūṣa."

sanskrit: seyaṃ panthānam āvārya vasaty atyardhayojane ata eva ca gantavyaṃ tāṭakāyā vanaṃ yataḥ
english: "She dwells there blocking the road, at a distance of more than a half-yojana; it is for that very reason that we must go to the forest of Tāṭakā."

sanskrit: svabāhubalam āśritya jahīmāṃ duṣṭacāriṇīm manniyogād imaṃ deśaṃ kuru niṣkaṇṭakaṃ punaḥ
english: "Relying on the strength of your own arms, slay this wicked creature, and at my command make this region free of thorns once more."

sanskrit: na hi kaś cid imaṃ deśaṃ śakroty āgantum īdṛśam yakṣiṇyā ghorayā rāma utsāditam asahyayā
english: "For no one is able to enter this region as it is, O Rāma, laid waste by that dreadful and irresistible yakṣiṇī."

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathaitad daruṇaṃ vanam yakṣyā cotsāditaṃ sarvam adyāpi na nivartate
english: "All of this has been told to you — how this forest became terrible, and how everything laid waste by the yakṣī has not recovered even to this day."

sanskrit: atha tasyāprameyasya muner vacanam uttamam śrutvā puruṣaśārdūlaḥ pratyuvāca śubhāṃ giram
english: Then, having heard the excellent words of that sage of immeasurable greatness, the tiger among men spoke an auspicious reply.

sanskrit: alpavīryā yadā yakṣāḥ śrūyante munipuṃgava kathaṃ nāgasahasrasya dhārayaty abalā balam
english: "When yakṣas are said to be of little power, O foremost of sages, how does this weak woman bear the strength of a thousand elephants?"

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'bravīd vākyaṃ śṛṇu yena balottarā varadānakṛtaṃ vīryaṃ dhārayaty abalā balam
english: Viśvāmitra spoke: "Hear by what means, though weak, she bears that superior strength — the valour wrought by the granting of a boon."

sanskrit: pūrvam āsīn mahāyakṣaḥ suketur nāma vīryavān anapatyaḥ śubhācāraḥ sa ca tepe mahat tapaḥ
english: "Formerly there was a great yakṣa named Suketu, valiant and of good conduct, who was childless; and he performed great austerity."

sanskrit: pitāmahas tu suprītas tasya yakṣapates tadā kanyāratnaṃ dadau rāma tāṭakāṃ nāma nāmataḥ
english: "The Pitāmaha (Brahmā) was greatly pleased with that lord of yakṣas and gave him a jewel of a daughter, O Rāma, named Tāṭakā."

sanskrit: dadau nāgasahasrasya balaṃ cāsyāḥ pitāmahaḥ na tv eva putraṃ yakṣāya dadau brahmā mahāyaśāḥ
english: "The Pitāmaha also gave her the strength of a thousand elephants; but Brahmā of great renown did not grant a son to that yakṣa."

sanskrit: tāṃ tu jātāṃ vivardhantīṃ rūpayauvanaśālinīm jambhaputrāya sundāya dadau bhāryāṃ yaśasvinīm
english: "That illustrious daughter, as she grew, resplendent with beauty and youth, was given as wife to Sunda, the son of Jambha."

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālalsya yakṣī putraṃ vyajāyata mārīcaṃ nāma durdharṣaṃ yaḥ śāpād rākṣaso 'bhavat
english: "Then, in the course of time, the yakṣī gave birth to a son named Mārīca, who was irresistible and who became a rākṣasa by a curse."

sanskrit: sunde tu nihate rāma agastyam ṛṣisattamam tāṭakā saha putreṇa pradharṣayitum icchati
english: "But when Sunda was slain, O Rāma, Tāṭakā, together with her son, sought to assault the most excellent of sages, Agastya."

sanskrit: rākṣasatvaṃ bhajasveti mārīcaṃ vyājahāra saḥ agastyaḥ paramakruddhas tāṭakām api śaptavān
english: "Agastya, in extreme fury, pronounced a curse on Mārīca saying 'Become a rākṣasa!'; and he also cursed Tāṭakā."

sanskrit: puruṣādī mahāyakṣī virūpā vikṛtānanā idaṃ rūpam apahāya dāruṇaṃ rūpam astu te
english: "'O great yakṣī who devours men, ugly and disfigured of face — abandoning this form, let a dreadful form be yours!'"

sanskrit: saiṣā śāpakṛtāmarṣā tāṭakā krodhamūrchitā deśam utsādayaty enam agastyacaritaṃ śubham
english: "She — this very Tāṭakā — enraged by the curse, senseless with fury, lays waste this region, once made auspicious by Agastya's dwelling in it."

sanskrit: enāṃ rāghava durvṛttāṃ yakṣīṃ paramadāruṇām gobrāhmaṇahitārthāya jahi duṣṭaparākramām
english: "Slay her, O Rāghava — this wicked, most dreadful yakṣī of evil prowess — for the welfare of cattle and brahmins."

sanskrit: na hy enāṃ śāpasaṃsṛṣṭāṃ kaś cid utsahate pumān nihantuṃ triṣu lokeṣu tvām ṛte raghunandana
english: "For no man is able to slay her who is bound by the curse, in the three worlds, except you, O joy of the Raghu line."

sanskrit: na hi te strīvadhakṛte ghṛṇā kāryā narottama cāturvarṇyahitārthāya kartavyaṃ rājasūnunā
english: "You must feel no scruple on account of the slaying of a woman, O best of men — a king's son must do what is needed for the welfare of the four social orders."

sanskrit: rājyabhāraniyuktānām eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ adharmyāṃ jahi kākutstha dharmo hy asyā na vidyate
english: "This is the eternal duty of those charged with the burden of kingship. Slay the unrighteous one, O Kākutstha — for righteousness does not exist in her."

sanskrit: śrūyate hi purā śakro virocanasutāṃ nṛpa pṛthivīṃ hantum icchantīṃ mantharām abhyasūdayat
english: "For it is told that in former times, O prince, Śakra slew Mantharā, the daughter of Virocana, when she sought to destroy the earth."

sanskrit: viṣṇunā ca purā rāma bhṛgupatnī dṛḍhavratā anindraṃ lokam icchantī kāvyamātā niṣūditā
english: "And formerly, O Rāma, Viṣṇu slew the wife of Bhṛgu, Kāvya's mother, firm in her vows, when she sought to make a world without Indra."

sanskrit: etaiś cānyaiś ca bahubhī rājaputramahātmabhiḥ adharmaniratā nāryo hatāḥ puruṣasattamaiḥ
english: "By these and many other great-souled royal heroes, women devoted to unrighteousness have been slain by the best of men."
